items.example: I have no idea. He just disappeared.
items.exampleTr: Hiçbir fikrim yok. Birden ortadan kayboldu.
items.simple: You say this when you do not know the answer at all.
dialogue: A: Where is Dan? His desk is empty.
B: I have no idea. He just disappeared.

items.example: I can't believe it. We won!
items.simple: You say this when something is so big you think it is not real.
dialogue: A: Look at the score on the screen!
B: I can't believe it. We won!

items.example: Give me a break. I only came late once.
items.exampleTr: Bırak ya. Sadece bir kez geç kaldım.
items.simple: You say this when someone is too hard on you.
dialogue: A: You are always late, Ben.
B: Give me a break. I only came late once.

items.example: Cut it out. That's my sandwich.
items.simple: You say this to tell someone to stop doing something that annoys you.
dialogue: A: Mmm, I am just taking a little bite.
B: Cut it out. That's my sandwich.
items.note: Malcolm in the Middle'da kardeşler arası.

items.example: Knock it off. Both of you, stop.
items.simple: Another way to say "stop it".
dialogue: A: He is pulling my hair, Mum!
B: Knock it off. Both of you, stop.

items.example: What's your problem? I said sorry!
items.simple: You ask this when someone is rude or angry with you.
dialogue: A: You are such a clumsy person.
B: What's your problem? I said sorry!
items.note: Brooklyn Nine-Nine ve Malcolm in the Middle'da kavgada.

items.example: Who cares? It's only a game.
items.simple: You say this when you think something is not important.
dialogue: A: But we lost the match!
B: Who cares? It's only a game.
items.note: Seinfeld ve Malcolm in the Middle'da.

items.example: Big deal. I'll buy another one.
items.exampleTr: Ne var yani? Bir tane daha alırım.
items.simple: You say this when you think something is not a problem. It can sound rude.
dialogue: A: You broke my favourite cup!
B: Big deal. I'll buy another one.
items.note: Alaycı tonda sık; ciddi "big deal" de var.

items.example: I told you so. It was too hot.
items.simple: You say this when you warned someone and it happened.
dialogue: A: Ow! I burned my tongue on the soup.
B: I told you so. It was too hot.

items.example: Since when do you like jazz?
items.simple: You ask this when you are surprised about a new thing.
dialogue: A: I bought two tickets for the jazz night.
B: Since when do you like jazz?
items.note: Brooklyn Nine-Nine ve HIMYM'de şaşkın soru.

items.example: Let it go. It was a long time ago.
items.simple: You say this to tell someone to forget a bad thing.
dialogue: A: He still has not said sorry to me.
B: Let it go. It was a long time ago.

items.example: Don't be like that. I said sorry.
items.simple: You say this when someone is cold or angry with you.
dialogue: A: I do not want to talk to you.
B: Don't be like that. I said sorry.

items.example: I drove you home. You owe me.
items.simple: You say this when you did a favour and want one back.
dialogue: A: Thanks for the lift last night!
B: I drove you home. You owe me.

items.example: That's what I'm saying. It's too loud.
items.exampleTr: Ben de bunu söylüyorum! Çok gürültülü.
items.simple: You say this when someone says the same thing as you.
dialogue: A: This music is too loud for a meeting.
B: That's what I'm saying. It's too loud.

items.example: What was that about? She looked angry.
items.simple: You ask this after something strange happened.
dialogue: A: Lisa just walked out of the room.
B: What was that about? She looked angry.

items.example: You're being weird. What's wrong?
items.simple: You say this when a person acts strangely.
dialogue: A: Why are you hiding behind the door?
B: You're being weird. What's wrong?
items.note: Friends ve The Big Bang Theory'de.

items.example: Hang in there. It gets better.
items.simple: You say this to help someone who has a hard time.
dialogue: A: Work is so hard this month.
B: Hang in there. It gets better.

items.example: I'm not kidding. He's really here.
items.simple: You say this when you are serious and want to be believed.
dialogue: A: Your old teacher is here? Come on!
B: I'm not kidding. He's really here.

items.example: Long story. I'll tell you later.
items.simple: You say this when you do not want to explain now.
dialogue: A: Why is there a goat in your garden?
B: Long story. I'll tell you later.

items.example: Not a chance. I'm not singing.
items.simple: You say this when you will never do it.
dialogue: A: Will you sing at my wedding?
B: Not a chance. I'm not singing.

items.example: I'm so over it. Let's move on.
items.simple: You say this when you do not feel anything about it any more.
dialogue: A: Are you still upset about your ex?
B: I'm so over it. Let's move on.

items.example: Not my problem. Ask Dave.
items.simple: You say this when it is not your job to fix it.
dialogue: A: The printer is broken again.
B: Not my problem. Ask Dave.

items.example: What are you doing here? It's midnight!
items.simple: You ask this when you are surprised to see someone.
dialogue: A: Surprise! I came to see you.
B: What are you doing here? It's midnight!

items.example: You look great. New haircut?
items.simple: A nice thing to say about how someone looks.
dialogue: A: Hi, it is so good to see you!
B: You look great. New haircut?

items.example: It was so awkward at dinner.
items.simple: Not comfortable. You do not know what to say or do.
dialogue: A: How was dinner with his parents?
B: It was so awkward at dinner.
items.note: The Office'in imzası; "awkward silence" çok sık.
